page.title: Best 200 Watt Solar Panel (2026): Tested Output and Price per Watt
page.desc: Tested output, price per watt and owner complaints for 200 W solar panels: the JJN bifacial for roofs, Renogy for folding, BougeRV for curved roofs.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 200 watt solar panel is the JJN 200W N-type Bifacial ({buy:jjnsolar-200w-n-type-bifacial-solar-panel}): JJN's bifacial 200 W panel made 182 W of its 200 W rating in OutdoorGearLab's 12-panel test, the highest share of any panel there, and it costs about 75 cents a rated watt. No 200 W panel makes 200 W in real use. In that test, the 12 tested panels made 112 to 193 W over two hours of clear sun, and owners report 140 to 160 W on a typical clear day.

The JJN is a rigid glass panel of about 25 lb, made to bolt to an RV roof, van rack, shed or ground stand. If you need a panel that folds for camping with a power station, buy the Renogy 200W Portable instead: it made 177 W in the same test and weighs 14.8 lb. For a curved roof, the BougeRV Arch 200W flexible panel weighs 6.6 lb and made 166 W, but flexible panels run hotter and carry shorter warranties.

OutdoorGearLab tested JJN's earlier bifacial 200W. JJN now sells it with N-type cells and a 30-year performance warranty. We have not seen an independent test of the N-type version.

rows.model: BougeRV Arch 200W Flexible (now sold as Arch 2.0)

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Less than 200 W (6 of 10 sources). Panel ratings are lab numbers. Expect 140 to 180 W at midday in clear sun, and less when it's hot or hazy or the panel lies flat. If you see under about 70% of the rating in full sun, check shade, angle and wiring before blaming the panel.
  • Glass broken on arrival (5 sources). This hits JJN and Renogy alike. One JJN buyer had 1 of 6 panels arrive shattered, and another had 2 of 3 orders damaged. Open the box, test the panel the day it arrives, and photograph any damage.
  • Short or awkward leads (3 sources). Rigid panels come with short MC4 pigtails, and OutdoorGearLab found the JJN's MC4 plugs hard to separate. Budget for an MC4 extension cable.
  • Wrong controller (3 sources). A "12 V" 200 W panel puts out roughly 22 to 28 V open-circuit. That works with a 12 V battery through a PWM or MPPT controller. Two panels in series can exceed a small PWM controller's limit, though, and cold mornings push the voltage higher still.
  • Fit on the roof (2 sources). A 200 W rigid panel is about 54 × 30 in. Measure the space between your vents and air conditioner first.

Which one by need

  • RV, van or shed roof, lowest cost: the JJN 200W N-type Bifacial. Its earlier version tested best of 12, and it costs less than BougeRV's rigid bifacial 200 W.
  • Folding panel for a power station: the Renogy 200W Portable. It made 177 W, weighs 14.8 lb and folds to 23.7 × 23.0 in.
  • Curved roof or no drilling: the BougeRV Arch 200W flexible panel (166 W, 6.6 lb). Mount it on battens so air can reach the back.
  • Bigger shed, cabin or ground array: the JJN 425W N-type Bifacial ({buy:jjnsolar-425w-n-type-bifacial-solar-panel}). Four panels give 1,700 W for about 67 cents a watt. It needs an MPPT controller or a power station with a high-voltage solar input.

Not recommended

  • Grecell 200W Portable and Marbero 200W Portable: they made 112 W and 134 W of their 200 W rating in OutdoorGearLab's test.
  • Gluing a flexible panel flat to a hot roof: Victron cites 2 to 15% less output than a rigid panel with air underneath. Flexible panels usually carry 1- to 3-year product warranties, against 10 to 12 years for rigid panels.

notes: QUERY: 'best 200 watt solar panel'. Google autocomplete today suggested it along with 'for rv', 'for camping', 'for the money' and 'reddit'. The pages answering it today are thin: undated affiliate roundups (thewearify, solarreviews 'in 2024', foliumbiosciences) built from listing specs. OutdoorGearLab's 12-panel test is the only measured comparison. PAIN POINTS (10 sources): output below the rating 6 (OGL table, two Van Living Forum threads, Renogy owner review via search, RV Outfitting, ShopSavvy); glass broken on arrival 5 (ShopSavvy 'numerous' for Renogy, Sienna Solar JJN 1 of 6, another JJN buyer 2 of 3 orders, desertcart JJN 'shattered' with good support, RV Outfitting); short or awkward MC4 leads 3; controller or voltage mismatch 3 (ShopSavvy '12V listed but 23V', solar-electric forum, GoodSam); roof fit around vents 2; failures around 10-12 months or slow warranty handling 1 (RV Outfitting). SEGMENTS AND WINNERS: (1) fixed mount on RV, van or shed, best value: JJN 200W bifacial. Its earlier version measured 182/200 W (91%), the best ratio of the 12 panels, with OGL's lowest cost per measured watt. It sells for $149 per panel vs BougeRV's rigid 16BB bifacial from $188.99. (2) folding panel for a power station: Renogy 200W Portable (177 W, 14.8 lb, OGL Editors' Choice). It is sold on Renogy and Amazon, not an approved program, so it gets a named row with a maker URL and no buy link. EcoFlow NextGen 220W made more raw output (193 W) but lists around $649. (3) curved roof: BougeRV Arch 200W flexible (166 W, 6.6 lb, OGL Top Pick), maker URL only. No approved CJ/Awin brand beats Renogy for folding or BougeRV for flexible. VERIFIED 2026-11-14: JJN 425W Updated Packaging variants ($315 for 1, $589 for 2, $869 for 3, $1,144 for 4, all available) via storecheck product, plus its listing text (16BB N-type, IP68, UL certified, 30-year performance warranty). JJN 200W N-type listing via storecheck search: lowest price $149.00, available. Its text says packs run from a single 200 W panel up to 10 panels (2,000 W), lists 12/24/48 V compatibility, IP68 junction box and a 30-year performance warranty. BougeRV prices (16BB bifacial from $188.99, Arch 2.0 from $229.99) are lowest-variant prices from storecheck search today. NOT VERIFIED: the JJN 200W product endpoint returned HTTP 429 all session (several runs share this IP), so I could not see the per-variant breakdown. I take $149 as the single-panel price because it is the listing's lowest variant price and the listing says packs start at one panel. A reviewer should confirm with one product read before publishing. Also not verified: JJN's return policy and product (workmanship) warranty term (OGL says 5 years, SolarReviews says 18 months, the listing gives only the 30-year performance term); JJN 200W N-type dimensions, weight and Voc (the page uses OGL's tested-unit figures, labeled as such); the 425W's weight and Voc; Renogy prices (none printed); any code printed on JJN's own US site (the homepage wasn't readable, so no brand-site code is listed). HONESTY CAVEAT: OGL tested JJN's earlier bifacial 200W (23% cells, Voc 28.1 V, ASIN B09VS7PR2J). The store now sells an N-type 16BB version, and the page says plainly that the N-type version has no independent test. JJN also sells a 200W Portable bifacial suitcase ($259.99, store search today).
